basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 7.' and it opens '(Vers. 7 et 8.) Et concepit adhuc, et peperit Bala ancilla Rachel filium secundum Jacob:'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Vers. 7 et 8.) Et concepit adhuc, et peperit Bala ancilla Rachel filium secundum Jacob: et dixit Rachel: Habitare fecit me Deus habitatione cum sorore mea, et invalui: et vocavit nomen ejus Nephthalim. Causam nominis Nephthalim, alia hic multo exponitur, quam in libro Hebraeorum Nominum scripta est. Unde et Aquila ait, συνανέστρεψέν με ὁ Θεὸς, καὶ συνανεστράφην, pro quo in Hebraeo scriptum est, NEPHTHULE ELOIM, NEPHTHALETHI. Unde a conversione, sive a comparatione, quia utrumque sonat, conversionem, sive comparationem, Nephthalim nomen filio imposuit. Quod autem sequitur.
